messages:
Priya: heads up - our new edge sample crashes during worker startup when importing the SDK. stack shows an ESM parsing error.
Ken: which runtime? Cloudflare, Deno, Vercel?
Priya: Cloudflare Pages Functions and local wrangler test. error: `SyntaxError: Unexpected token 'export'` pointing at node_modules/@redwood/sdk/dist/index.js
Aziza: that typically means a CJS file being treated as ESM or vice-versa. Do we publish mixed outputs?
Priya: yes, package builds cjs+esm and package.json has "type": "module" in the sample repo, but SDK package has both main + module fields. tsserver in the sample also shows types are fuzzy - overloaded functions appearing as `any`.
Sam: Repro'd locally. tsconfig in sample was `target: es2020, module: ESNext, moduleResolution: Node`, bundler is esbuild with default conditions.
Ken: quick check: is the sample importing a subpath like `@redwood/sdk/client`? TS resolves subpath types differently, sometimes picks the root d.ts if not exported in `typesVersions`.
Priya: import is `import { createClient } from '@redwood/sdk'`. I tried forcing alias to `/dist/esm/index.mjs` in esbuild and that fixed runtime, but editor still lost overload detail.
Aziza: editor type loss could be because the .d.ts that tsserver loads doesn't line up with runtime entry. Two fixes: 1) use conditional exports with explicit subpath types mapping, or 2) add `typesVersions` in package.json so TS maps imports to the right d.ts based on module resolution.
Ken: +1 on typesVersions. Example snippet: 
```json
"typesVersions": {"*": {"*": ["dist/esm/*", "dist/*"]}}
```
but that only helps if you emit per-subpath `.d.ts` files.
Priya: we only emit a single `dist/index.d.ts`. can we produce per-format shims like `dist/esm/index.d.ts` that re-export the root types?
Sam: yes, we can ship small .d.ts forwarding files. Also consider adding `.mjs`/`.cjs` extensions to outputs to avoid ambiguity for runtimes that enforce ESM.
Aziza: regarding overloads collapsing: I looked at the SDK signatures. There's an overload chain `createClient<T>(config: Config<T>)` and a fallback `createClient(config: any)`. TS will pick `any` if inference can't satisfy the generic. Avoiding a raw `any` fallback helps. Consider `unknown` fallback and add an overload with a constrained generic up front.
Ken: another approach: export a typed factory `createClient` with a helper generic like `as const` on configs in our docs to help inference. but we should fix the surface types.
Priya: I'm worried about breaking older Node consumers if we switch main/module. We need to be careful with export map. Suggest: publish export map with explicit keys: `.` -> import/cjs and `./package.json`, and include `types` at root. Example: 
```json
"exports": {
  ".": {
    "import": "./dist/esm/index.mjs",
    "require": "./dist/cjs/index.cjs"
  },
  "./*": "./dist/*"
}
"types": "dist/index.d.ts"
```
This keeps TS happy if we also emit `dist/esm/index.d.ts` re-exporting the root declarations.
Aziza: also add a small `tests/ts-compat/edge.ts` that imports the SDK and asserts overload behavior using `expectType` from `tsd` or `dtslint` in CI matrix. We'll run across node14/node18 + bundler vs tsc-only configs.
Sam: opened a tiny repro repo and PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-repros/edge-exports-176888 (branch "exports-fix"). includes scripts to build SDK locally and link into sample.
CI-Bot: CI check: sdk unit tests passed, edge-sample build failed on matrix item node:14 due to .mjs not supported there (see job 521).
Ken: for Node14 we should still emit cjs `.cjs` files and keep require entry. export map handles that. runtime pick should be fine.
Aziza: typing follow-up - I'll rework overloads to remove `any` fallback and add a constrained generic + overload ordering. Also add a simple `index.d.ts` with explicit overloads in the dist output to ensure tsc sees them.
Priya: Docs for sample need a blurb: when running on edge, prefer explicit esm alias or use the `exports`-aware bundler settings: 
```
// esbuild example
build({ conditions: ['worker', 'import'] })
```
and an alias to `@redwood/sdk/dist/esm` if necessary.
Sam: action items: 1) Aziza will send typing PR removing `any` fallback + add d.ts shims, 2) Ken will update CI to run `tsc --noEmit` in sdk matrix with multiple tsconfigs, 3) Priya will update sample README and add esbuild snippet, 4) I'll follow up on fixation for node14 support in PR.
Priya: thanks all. marking resolved unless someone sees an urgent blocker. will reopen if CI shows regressions. :smile:
